This document will go over the high level UI specifications for the web
validation tool. These specifications are not meant to specify the **visual**
aspects of the tool (i.e. they are not meant to be pretty) but are more meant
to specify functional aspects of the UI.

The specifications will go through each feature outlined in the high level
specifications and explain their functional aspects by using wireframe
diagrams as well as flow diagrams.

# Screen Types

The different screens that are part of the UI can be broadly classified into
pages and dialogs.

Pages allow the user to perform a variety of actions while also showing
information based on the current context. For example, the
[view dataset page](#view-dataset-page) shows the user information about a
dataset, but also allows them to perform actions like uploading a new dataset,
starting a new
validation etc. Pages consist of three main components:
1. [Top Bar](#top-bar): Has actions that can be done from any page.
2. [Sidebar](#sidebar): Has actions relevant to the current page. Currently, the
   sidebar is populated with common actions that the user can perform on a
   selected dataset.
3. Content: Has information for the current page along with any additional
   context specific actions.

Dialogs are used when a process cannot be completed in a single step (for e.g.,
[uploading a dataset](#dataset-upload), or for actions that require
confirmation from a user. They are overlaid on top of a page, and a user is not
allowed to interact with the page until the dialog is closed.

# Features

Each of the next sub-sections will go over the features for the tool and the
user flows and/or wireframes for them. The sections that show flow diagrams
will not go through each page in the flow, those can be seen in the
[screens](#screens) section.

## [Dataset Upload](../spec.qmd#dataset-upload)

There are multiple pages from which a user can start the process of uploading
a dataset, this section will focus on the home page as the starting point.
The image below contains the flow diagram for uploading a dataset from the home
page.

![upload dataset from the home page](../../dist/upload-dataset-from-home-page.png)

The user can initiate the upload dataset flow by clicking on the **Upload
Dataset** button from any page where its available.

In addition, the user should not be allowed to proceed from the **Configure
Dataset** dialog unless all the dataset metadata is valid.

This flow can also be initiated from the
[Validation Summary](#from-the-validation-summary-page) page and
[View Dataset](#from-the-view-dataset-page) page. The flows are identical to the
one above, with the only difference being the start page.

### Uploading a Duplicate Dataset

The red arrows in the above image represents the flow when the user uploads the
same dataset as an existing one. Two datasets are considered the same when they
have the same file names.

Since users cannot edit their dataset within the tool, after validation, they
will need to reupload it in order to validate it again. By allowing users to
replace an existing dataset during the upload process, they can have a history
of all the previous validations done on the different versions of the same
dataset.

## [Upload Report](../spec.qmd#upload-report)

The user can view the upload report from the [View Dataset](#view-dataset-page)
page. The two ways the user can access this page is by:

1. Successfully uploading a new dataset which takes them to the page; and
2. Clicking on an already uploaded dataset which can be done from the
   [Validation Summary](#validation-summary-page) page or the
   [View Dataset](#view-dataset-page) page.

# Screens

The next sub-sections will go over the different pages and dialogs presented in
the flow diagrams above.

## Home Page

![home page](../../dist/home-page.png)

The home page is shown to the user when they open the tool. From the home
page they can:

* Perform an action from the [top bar](#top-bar)

## Upload Dataset Dialog

![upload dataset dialog](../../dist/upload-dataset-dialog.png)

This dialog is part of the [upload dataset flow](#dataset-upload)
where the user can upload a CSV or Excel file to the tool. 

From this dialog the user can:

* Upload a CSV or Excel file to the tool by clicking on the text or dragging and 
  dropping a file. When the text is clicked, it should bring up the browser's 
  [native file chooser](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/file).
  * Once the user has uploaded the file the text should be replaced with the 
    name of the uploaded file. This gives feedback to the user that their file 
    has been uploaded.
* Confirm their uploaded file by pressing the Ok button. The button should be 
  disabled until the user uploads a file.
* Close the dialog by clicking the Cancel button.

## Configure Dataset Dialog

Depending on the dataset that the user wants to configure, a different
dialog is shown.

### Configure CSV Dataset Dialog

![Configure CSV dataset dialog](../../dist/configure-csv-dataset-dialog.png)

In this dialog the user can:

* Select the ODM version that this dataset is for. This is the **ODM version**
  dropdown. Refer to the high level specifications for what versions the tool
  supports.
* Select the ODM table that this dataset represents. This is done using the
  **Table** dropdown.
* Save the configuration by clicking the **Save** button.
* Cancel the configuration by clicking the **Close** button.

In addition,

* The ** \<CSV file name\> ** text should be replaced with the file name of the
  dataset.
* The user should be allowed to save the configuration only if the ODM version
  and table dropdown have been correctly filled in.

### Configure Excel Dataset Dialog

![configure excel dataset dialog](../../dist/configure-excel-dataset-dialog.png)

From this dialog the user can:

* Choose the ODM version the dataset is for. This is done using the **ODM
  version** dropdown. For the list of supported ODM versions, look at the high
  level specifications.
* Choose the ODM table that each sheet maps to. This is done using the dropdowns
  at the bottom of the **Tables** text.
* Save the configuration by clicking the **Save** button.
* Cancel the configuration by clicking the **Close** button.

In addition,

* The ** \<Excel file name\> ** text should be replaced with the file name of the
  dataset
* The user should be allowed to save the configuration only if the ODM version
  and table dropdowns have been correctly filled in.

## View Dataset Page

![view dataset page](../../dist/view-dataset-page.png)

This page is shown when the user uploads a new dataset or selects a dataset
on another page. It allows the user to view summary details about the
uploaded dataset.

From this page the user can:

* Perform an action from the [top bar](#top-bar)
* View the **Upload Report** which summarizes the uploaded dataset.
* Perform an action from the [sidebar](#sidebar)

## Validation Summary Page

![validation summary page](../../dist/validation-summary-page.png)

This page provides summary for a particular dataset validation. From this
page the user can:

* Perform an action from the [top bar](#top-bar)
* View the upload report for the selected validation
* View the entire validation report by clicking the **Validation Report** button
* Perform an action from the [sidebar](#sidebar)

## New Validation Dialog

![new validation dialog](../../dist/new-validation-dialog.png)

This dialog is used by the user to start a new validation and is part of the
[validate dataset](#dataset-validation) flow.

From this dialog the user can:

* Choose the validation profile they want to use using the **validation
  profile** dropdown
* View the properties of their selected profile using the **Validation
  Properties** panel
* Customize the validation by creating a new profile. This is done by clicking
  the **Customize Validation** button
* Start the validation by clicking the **Start Validation** button
* Cancel the new validation by clicking the **Cancel** button

In addition,

* By default the selected validation profile should be one created by the
  ODM staff

## Validating Dialog

![validating dialog](../../dist/validating-dialog.png)

This dialog is part of the [validate dataset](#dataset-validation) flow.

From this dialog the user can:

* View their validation progress
* Cancel the validation by pressing the **Cancel** button

## Cancel Validation Dialog

![cancel validation dialog](../../dist/cancel-validation-dialog.png)

This dialog is part of the [validate dataset](#dataset-validation) flow. Its
used to confirm with the user if they want to cancel their validation.

From this dialog the user can:

* Cancel the validation process by clicking the **Yes** button
* Continue the validation process by clicking the **Not** button

## View Validation Profiles Dialog

![view validation profiles dialog](../../dist/view-validation-profiles-dialog.png)

From this dialog the user can:

* View the different validation profiles they have
* Edit any one by clicking the **Edit** button
* Download any one by clicking the **Download** button
* Delete any one by clocking the **Delete** button
* Create a new profile by clicking the **Create New Profile** button
* Return to the previous page by clicking the **Close** button

## Create Validation Profile Dialog

![create validation profile dialog](../../dist/create-validation-profile-dialog.png)

From this dialog the user can:

* Edit the name of their new validation profile. This field is mandatory.
* Edit the description of their new validation profile. This field is optional.
* Edit the rules they want to be part of this profile. At least one rule should
  be selected.
* Create the new profile by clicking the **Create Profile** button. The above
  validations need to pass for the profile creation.
* Create a new profile by uploading a validation profile. When they upload the
  file, the tool should attempt to fill in the fields using the information in
  the file. This is done using the **Upload Profile** button.
* Cancel the creation with the **Cancel** button.

## Edit Validation Profile Dialog

![edit validation profile dialog](../../dist/edit-validation-profile-dialog.png)

This dialog has the same functionality as the
[Create Validation Profile](#create-validation-profile-dialog) dialog.

## Delete Validation Profile Dialog

![delete validation profile dialog](../../dist/delete-validation-profile-dialog.png)

Used to confirm if the user wants to delete a validation profile. From this
dialog the user can:

* Confirm they want to delete a validation profile by clicking the **Yes**
  button
* Stop the deletion by clicking the **No** button

## Choose Validation Profile Dialog

![choose validation profile dialog](../../dist/choose-validation-profile-dialog.png)

When uploading a validation profile, this dialog allows the user to choose a
validation profile file from their computer. It should use the
[File Dialog](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/file)
provided by the browser.

## Validation Report Dialog

![view validation report dialog](../../dist/validation-report-dialog.png)

From this dialog the user can:

* View the full results of a validation
* Download the validation report by clicking on one of the options in the
  **Download Report** dropdown.
* Set what they want to include in the downloaded report by using the **Download
  Options** dropdown.
* Close the validation report by clicking the **Close** button

## Duplicate Dataset Dialog

![duplicate dataset dialog](../../dist/duplicate-dataset-dialog.png)

This dialog is shown during the [dataset upload](#dataset-upload) flow when the
user tries to upload a file with the same name as an existing dataset.

The `<File Name>` text should be replaced with the name of the duplicate dataset.
From this dialog the user can:

* Choose to update the dataset by clicking the **Update the Dataset** button
* Choose to replace the dataset by clicking the **Replace the Dataset** button

## Replace Dataset Confirm Dialog

![replace dataset confirm dialog](../../dist/replace-dataset-confirm-dialog.png)

This dialog is shown during the [dataset upload](#dataset-upload) flow to
confirm that user wants to replace an existing dataset.

From this dialog the user can:

* Choose to not replace the existing dataset by clicking the **No** button
* Choose to replace the existing dataset by clicking the **Yes** button

# UI Components

This section contains UI components that are used in multiple pages and/or
dialogs.

## Top Bar

The top bar is used in the [Home Page](#home-page),
[View Dataset](#view-dataset-page), and [Validation Summary](#validation-summary-page)
pages. Its affixed to the top and contains actions that can be done from all
these pages.

![top bar](../../dist/top-bar.png)

From the top bar the user can:

* Upload a new dataset by clicking on the **Upload Dataset** button
* Navigate to the [View Dataset](#view-dataset-page) page by clicking on one
  of the items in the **Datasets** dropdown.
* View their validation profiles by clicking on the **View Validation Profiles**
  button
* View the tutorials by clicking the **Tutorials** button

## Sidebar

The sidebar is used in the [View Dataset](#view-dataset-page) and
[Validation Summary](#validation-summary-page) pages. It shows user actions
for a particular dataset.

There are two versions of the sidebar depending on whether there are
[multiple versions](#uploading-a-duplicate-dataset) of the current dataset as
shown below:

![sidebar with a single dataset version](../../dist/sidebar-no-multiple-versions.png)

![sidebar with multiple dataset versions](../../dist/sidebar-multiple-versions.png)

From the sidebar the user can:

* Configure the currently selected dataset by clicking the **Configure
  Dataset** button
* View their previous validations by clicking on one of them in the
  **Previous Validations** section.
  * If there are multiple versions of a dataset then:
    * The previous validations should be presented grouped by the dataset
      version they belong to.
    * The groupings should be in reverse chronological order, i.e. the
      latest uploaded dataset version should be presented first.
    * If a dataset version has only one previous validation, it should not be
      grouped under the dataset version number. Instead, a button should be
      shown to the user whose text includes the version number and the
      validation title. For example, the v2 button shown in the above image.
    * If a dataset version has multiple previous validations, they should be
      grouped within the dataset version name. A button for each previous
      validation should be shown, with the name of the validation in the button
      text. For example, the v1 grouping shown in the above image.
* Start a new validation by clicking the **Validate Dataset** button
